sources.entry: ukncsc/zero-trust-architecture: Principles to help you design and deploy a zero trust architecture

summary.one_liner: A UK NCSC guidance document listing eight design principles for planning and deploying a zero trust architecture in enterprise environments.
summary.what_it_does: The README presents version 1.0 of the NCSC's zero trust architecture design principles, which are described as a companion to the authoritative guidance published on the NCSC website. It defines zero trust as removing inherent trust in the network, assuming it is hostile, and verifying each request against an access policy. The eight principles cover knowing your architecture (users, devices, services, data), giving every user, service and device a unique cryptographically identifiable identity, assessing behaviour and device/service health, authorising requests through policies, authenticating and authorising everywhere, focusing monitoring on users, devices and services, not trusting any network (including your own) and using secure transport, and choosing services designed for zero trust. The README also lists the intended audience (board readers, technical staff, and vendors or open source projects) and invites feedback through issues, pull requests, or email.
use_cases: designing a zero trust network architecture
reviewing an existing enterprise security architecture against zero trust principles
selecting zero trust products or services from vendors
briefing a board on zero trust concepts
planning identity and device verification for remote access
notable: Published by the UK National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) as v1.0 design principles
Eight numbered principles covering identity, policy, monitoring, network trust and service selection
Written for enterprise, public and private sector audiences, with separate guidance for board and technical readers
Repository is a community feedback channel; the website version is described as the authoritative text
caveats: The README is conceptual guidance only and names no tools, products or code to install
It states that the peer-reviewed authoritative version lives on the NCSC website, so this repo may lag or differ from it
Refers readers to separate introduction and ALPHA/BETA guidance pages whose links are not included in the README text
